answers.answer: Rule is based on warriors plus buildings in a clearing; a player must have more total than every other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Rule (2.5).

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of the player's warriors/pawns along a linking path to an adjacent clearing, and the player must rule the origin, destination, or both. Rule is rechecked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Move (4.2).

answers.answer: Battle order is Ambush, before-roll effects, roll, after-roll effects, count hits, deal hits. Defender may play one matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals none; otherwise defender immediately deals two hits, not capped by its warriors, and battle ends if the attacker has no warriors or pawns left. Higher die is attacker's rolled hits and lower die defender's (Alliance defending reverses dice); each side's rolled hits are capped by its own battle warriors, while Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead. At equal dice both deal equal results. Extra hits are added uncapped, ignored hits subtracted; a defender with no warriors gives the attacker one defenseless extra hit (Vagabond instead checks for undamaged swords). Each hit removes an opposing piece; its owner chooses order but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens, and also chooses order of its removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal their counted hits even if warriors were removed after the roll. The player removing an enemy building/token scores one VP each, whether attacker or defender and even outside battle.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3), six numbered steps.

answers.answer: Craft a hand card by activating crafting pieces matching its bottom-left crafting icons, not by paying its card suit. Each crafting piece activates once per turn, except Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted unless that item is in the map supply. An identical persistent effect already in the player's play area cannot be crafted again.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Craft (4.1).

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. You win at the start of your own Birdsong if you rule three clearings of the matching mouse/rabbit/fox suit, or, for bird dominance, both diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. An available bird dominance remains bird and must be paid for with a bird card; a bird hand card can pay for a non-bird dominance card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: With two players remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea and 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is in the game, put one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword under the four ruins, one per ruin; without Vagabond the ruins hold no items. Standard faction setup order is Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond, distinct from turn order. Alliance also draws three additional cards face down into Supporters (not its hand).
answers.evidence: Setup: steps 3–4 and faction setup order; Alliance and Vagabond setup.

answers.answer: Only Marquise may place pieces in its Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing rather than supply; this can happen outside battle. If the Keep is gone, there is no Field Hospitals destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6): Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts by crafting with workshops, then permits up to three actions plus one action for each bird card spent outside an action, in any order. March is one action of up to two moves; do not interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn; if supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the available maximum, choosing eligible recruiters. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6): Daylight actions.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing Marquise rules with an open building slot and a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost printed atop its column in wood, removing wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. Full cost, a building available on the track, and a legal slot are all required.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6): Build.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, first draw one card if hand is empty (Emergency Orders); then add one or two hand cards to Decree, with at most one bird card added; then, if there are no roosts on the map, place a roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7): Birdsong steps 1–3.

answers.answer: Eyrie crafts first with roosts, then resolves all Decree cards by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order. Within a column it chooses card order freely; bird cards are wild. Recruit places one warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic); Move moves at least one warrior from a matching clearing under ordinary move rules; Battle starts a battle in a matching clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build places a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any action cannot be fully completed, it immediately turmoils and cannot skip that card or continue other columns.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7): Daylight—resolve the Decree.

answers.answer: Turmoil costs one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are face up; retuck Viziers into the new leader's columns. Turmoil ends Daylight, but does not remove Eyrie map warriors or buildings. Evening still occurs: score the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, and discard to five.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7): Turmoil, in order; Evening.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. If there are no bases, the Supporters maximum is five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded; with a base there is no limit. Capacity still applies to Outrage additions.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8): Outrage; Supporters capacity.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, Alliance may take any number of Revolts first, then any number of Spread Sympathy actions. Revolt selects a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on the board, spends two matching Supporters, removes all enemy pieces there and scores one VP per enemy building/token removed, places that base, then places warriors equal to the number of matching-suit sympathetic clearings (including this one) and one warrior in Officers. Spread Sympathy selects an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; spends the matching Supporter cost shown above the next token, plus one matching Supporter under Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there; then places sympathy and scores the uncovered VP. Revolt scores for enemy buildings/tokens removed; Spread scores its token track VP and does not remove enemy pieces. Placement limits mean Revolt places as many prompted pieces as possible.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8): Birdsong—Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: In Daylight, Train spends a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. In Evening, Organize is one available military operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score its uncovered VP. It has no Supporter cost, adjacency requirement, or Martial Law cost, but needs legal token placement. If a base is removed, discard all Supporters matching its clearing including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard excess Supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8): Losing a base; Daylight Train; Evening Organize.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, Vagabond refreshes two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three additional exhausted items; tea refreshed during this step adds no refresh now. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out of a clearing. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if the destination has warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. Evening in a forest returns all damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if possible; this Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, including after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9): Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening steps.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track, score 1 VP if an item is taken, and remove the ruin once its last item is taken, freeing its slot. Quest exhausts the two listed items for a face-up quest matching the clearing, puts it in the play area, and chooses either VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards; it draws a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel without changing its face; ready tea/coins/bags move to their tracks if space is available.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9): Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes that faction Hostile, except for the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. On your own turn in battle, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; add ordinary VP for buildings/tokens. Infamy is not scored while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile relationship out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that faction has no warriors there may it instead remove another faction piece. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9): Relationships, Hostile, Infamy, Aid and Strike.

answers.answer: With four or more players, during Vagabond's own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with another player not already in a coalition. Choose the player with the lowest VP among the other players, choosing among ties. Put Vagabond's score marker on the partner's faction board and stop scoring; if the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including a dominance win. If the partner is Hostile, reset that relationship to Indifferent. Coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
